title: The Effects of Subjective Training Load Regulation Based on Menstrual Cycle Symptom Scores and Recovery–Stress Questionnaires on Adaptations in Body Composition and Muscular Strength in Young Menstruating Women
summary:
The aim of this study is to investigate how different methods of individually adjusting training loads affect muscle growth and maximal strength in resistance-trained women.

Participants will be assigned to one of four groups. Three groups will complete an eight-week structured full-body resistance training program consisting of three training sessions per week. In the first group, training loads will be adjusted based on daily assessments of menstrual cycle-related symptoms. In the second group, training loads will be adjusted according to participants' perceived levels of stress and recovery. The third group will follow a traditional linear resistance training program with predetermined increases in training loads. A fourth group will serve as a passive control group and will not participate in any additional resistance training as part of the study.

All participants will complete two daily questionnaires: one assessing menstrual cycle-related symptoms and another assessing perceived stress and recovery. Participants will not be informed which questionnaire is used to guide adjustments to their individual training loads.

Body composition and maximal strength will be assessed at the beginning and end of the eight-week study period. In addition, actual training intensity, training volume, and adherence to the prescribed training program will be recorded.

The study aims to determine whether individually adjusting resistance training loads based on menstrual cycle-related symptoms or perceived stress and recovery provides advantages over traditional resistance training in terms of muscle growth, strength development, and training adherence.
conditions: health eumenoheuric women with resistance training experience

interventions.name: Over an eight-week training period, the women's menstrual cycle symptom scores are assessed daily. On training days, their respective scores are taken into account to adjust the training intensity for that day.

Over an eight-week training period, the women's stress-recovery scores are assessed daily using a stress-recovery questionnaire. On training days, their respective scores are taken into account to adjust the training intensity for that day.
